verdict: Wise's product page is cited 1.63 times per fetch with 483 words and no comparison, no table and no prose. Skydo's four feature pages share one title, are fetched 877 times and cited 84 times in total (0.10). ChatGPT reaches product pages on vendor-check fanouts ('Wise India receive money business', 'site:skydo.com receive USD') and wants one page that states, under its own heading, what account details, what rate, what document, what time, who is eligible and what regulator. Wise's page is that list. Skydo's is a hero, a savings calculator and three benefit tiles.

diagnosis: Product pages are fetched on vendor-verification fanouts, after the brand is already shortlisted. ChatGPT is looking for attributes to quote, not persuasion.

One heading per entity-attribute pair with one sentence of value under it is the whole trick. Currency → account details; step 3 → deliverables; benefit → checkable fact; eligibility → reader types; regulator → status.
Skydo's feature pages have no heading elements, no paragraphs and no dates. The crawler sees a hero and tiles.
Four duplicate feature pages with one title split the fetches and give ChatGPT no reason to prefer any of them.
Skydo's fee FAQ page (1.01 per fetch, 996 citations) already proves the shape works on skydo.com: one question, one answer, the numbers.
The hero comparison ('10x less than PayPal') is unquotable; the eligibility block at the bottom is quotable and should be near the top.
The product page must not compare. The comparison already lives on the landing page and the compare pages, which win their buckets.
spec: Merge the four /features pages into one URL, e.g. /receive-money, with 301s from the others.
Title 'Receive international payments in India'. H1 the same.
One H2 per currency Skydo supports (USD: routing and account number; GBP: sort code and account number; EUR: IBAN; CAD; AUD; SGD; AED), one sentence each.
Three numbered steps ending 'INR in your Indian bank within 24 hours, FIRA in your dashboard'.
Three fact blocks as H2 + one sentence: live mid-market rate with zero markup; flat fee $19 up to $2,000, $29 to $10,000, 0.3% above, dated; FIRA free on every payment.
Eligibility H2 near the top: freelancers, sole proprietors, LLPs, Pvt Ltd; 'Skydo is not for' list kept.
Regulatory H2: 'RBI PA-CB final authorisation, January 2026'.
FAQ questions matching the objections: does my client need Skydo, which company types, limits, which countries, FIRA.
Under 700 words. No calculator, no competitor names, no comparison. Real HTML headings and paragraphs.

playbook.bucket: Vendor product page: what <brand> gives me
playbook.use_when: The fanout checks a vendor already on the shortlist: '<brand> India receive money business', 'site:<brand>.com receive USD', '<brand> FIRA', '<brand> eligibility'. ChatGPT wants attributes to quote under the brand's name.
blueprint: URL and title carry the job in the searcher's words: /receive-money, 'Receive international payments in India'.
One H2 per entity-attribute pair, one sentence under each. Currencies first: the exact account details you get per currency.
A numbered process whose last step names the deliverables (INR in bank, FIRA in inbox).
Benefit blocks as checkable facts: rate basis, document issued, time to settle, fee slabs with a date.
Eligibility statement naming reader types (freelancer, sole proprietor, LLP, Pvt Ltd) with a qualify link, and a 'not for' list.
Regulatory status in plain words: regulator, status, date.
FAQ questions that mirror objections: does my client need an account, who is eligible, limits, countries.
Under 700 words. Real HTML headings and paragraphs. No comparison, no competitor names, no calculator in the crawled text.
One URL per product job. Merge duplicates and 301 them.
